title: #help: how does inbound Gmail sync get triggered? trying to figure out why a test...
text:
Aisha Bello: how does inbound Gmail sync get triggered? trying to figure out why a test mailbox took a few minutes to show new emails
Dana Okafor: When Gmail or Microsoft pings our webhook, we enqueue one job that runs the list fetch for that channel right away. That's #26180. Before it, the webhook just flipped the channel to PENDING and waited up to 5 minutes for the cron, which is probably what you saw on an older build. Bursts of pings fold into one job through BullMQ dedup, so you don't get a pile of duplicate syncs. Deltas over 50 items are still left to the import cron.
Marcus Lee: The cron is the fallback for anything webhooks miss. Since #26181 each sync cron runs one cross-workspace query per tick instead of one per workspace, so it's cheap. If a channel looks stuck, check whether it's still waiting on the cron.
Aisha Bello: perfect, that explains it. thanks both
